title: How much does Ziva spend on lunch in five days?
description: Ziva spends the same money on each of five school days. Five equal lots are written as a times sentence, which is called an expression, and it is worked out to its value. Keeko doubts the sentence and adds the number of days to the money.
teaching_notes: One idea: equal lots become a times sentence, and the number it works out to is its value. Watch for children who add the number of days to the money instead of multiplying.

source: Ziva spends ₹25 every day for lunch at school. Write an expression for what is spent in 5 days and find its value.
video_script.why: The child meets an expression and its value through a spend that repeats.
video_script.substitution: Write the five equal payments as one times sentence, then work it out.
video_script.anchor: Ziva's lunch money for five school days, Monday to Friday
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko adds the number of days to the money to get 25 + 5 = 30. Five plates of 25 do not match thirty, so the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: Ziva spends one hundred and twenty five rupees in five days

final_answer.spoken: the expression is five times twenty five and its value is one hundred and twenty five rupees

names.Ziva: the child who spends 25 rupees on lunch each school day

maths_rules: Ziva spends 25 rupees a day on lunch, for 5 school days.
Five lots of 25 give the expression 5 × 25.
slip: 25 + 5 = 30, which adds the days to the money
book example for the words: the value of 13 + 2 is 15
video_script.design: One idea: equal lots become a times sentence; its value is what it works out to. Assumes multiplying equal lots. Wrong idea: add the days to the money. The five plates stay all video.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; Ziva at the canteen counter with a plate and 25 rupees in the anchor band

marks.book: the title card arrives: From your book
marks.spend: the line appears: Ziva spends ₹25 on lunch every school day
marks.ask: the days Monday to Friday light up one by one

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='spend'/>Ziva spends twenty five rupees on lunch every school day.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How can we write the money spent from Monday to Friday, and what does it come to?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: five plates each marked 25 appear in a row; a brace over them reads five lots of 25

marks.day: one plate marked 25 appears for each day
marks.lots: the brace over the five plates appears

narration: <bookmark mark='day'/>Each day is one lot of twenty five rupees.
<bookmark mark='lots'/>Five days make five equal lots of twenty five rupees.

beats.on_screen: the line 13 + 2 = 15 is written; the phrase 13 + 2 gets the label expression; the number 15 gets the label value

marks.expr: the label expression lands on the phrase 13 + 2
marks.val: the label value lands on the number 15

narration: <bookmark mark='expr'/>A phrase made of numbers and operation signs, such as thirteen plus two, is called an expression.
<bookmark mark='val'/>The number it works out to is called its value. The value of thirteen plus two is fifteen.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, Ziva spends twenty five rupees each day for five days.

beats.on_screen: To find: the expression and its value

marks.find: the words expression and value are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write an expression for the money spent in five days, and find its value.

marks.write: the times sentence 5 × 25 is written under the brace

narration: <bookmark mark='write'/>Step one, write the expression. Five equal lots of twenty five rupees are written five times twenty five, because multiplying counts equal lots.

marks.split: twenty five splits into twenty and five
marks.parts: the two partial products 100 and 25 are written

narration: <bookmark mark='split'/>Step two, work out the value. Split twenty five into twenty and five, because five times each part is quick to find.
<bookmark mark='parts'/>Five times twenty is one hundred, and five times five is twenty five.

marks.join: the two parts 100 and 25 join with a plus sign

narration: <bookmark mark='join'/>Step three, add the two parts, because five times twenty five is made of both of them.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Ziva spends one hundred and twenty five rupees in five days.
The expression is five times twenty five, and its value is one hundred and twenty five rupees.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 25 + 5 = 30; five plates of 25 beside it do not match; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.fix: the bubble is struck through and the five plates glow

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the total is twenty five plus five, which is thirty rupees.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But that adds the number of days to the money. The days only count the lots, so they cannot be added to the rupees.
